title: Algebraic topology
stage: Graduate study and qualifying exams in mathematics
audience: a graduate student in the first years of a mathematics PhD preparing for qualifying exams, or a graduate preparing to apply for one
purpose: Learn the main invariants of algebraic topology: homotopy and the fundamental group, van Kampen's theorem, covering spaces and their classification, cell complexes, simplicial and singular homology, exact sequences and excision, the Mayer–Vietoris sequence, cellular homology and the Euler characteristic, and classic applications such as the Brouwer fixed point theorem and degree theory.
primary_reading: Algebraic Topology by Allen Hatcher (free PDF)

weeks.1: Homotopy, homotopy equivalence and the fundamental group
weeks.2: The fundamental groups of the circle and the spheres
weeks.4: Cell complexes and their fundamental groups
weeks.5: Covering spaces and the lifting criterion
weeks.6: The classification of covering spaces and deck transformations
weeks.11: Cellular homology and the Euler characteristic
weeks.12: Applications: degree, fixed points and vector fields on spheres

blocks.deliverable: Compute the fundamental groups of supplied spaces.
Compute the fundamental group of a surface from its cell structure.
Find all connected covering spaces of a supplied space up to a given number of sheets.
Week 7 midterm; compute the simplicial homology of a supplied complex.
Compute the homology of spheres and surfaces with the Mayer–Vietoris sequence.
Prove the Brouwer fixed point theorem in every dimension from homology.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Qualifying-exam dossier in topology: write complete solutions to twenty exam-style problems on fundamental groups, covering spaces and homology, compute the homology of eight spaces by two methods where possible, write a plain-Python program that computes rational homology from a list of simplices by matrix ranks and use it to check your hand computations, and write a two-page summary of the main theorems with their hypotheses.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
